open_points.subject: operation execution disclosure class
open_points.text: A07 rule 5 defines an execution's class as "the highest class among the values and files its NodeExecution or TrialExecution names as inputs ... and for an operation also among its outputs" but gives no fallback when an operation has neither inputs nor outputs.
open_points.question: What disclosure class does an operation execution with no inputs and no outputs have, including for classifying its failure_detail?
options: open
the binding must be refused unless it has an input or output
some other fixed class

open_points.subject: redacted failure detail
open_points.text: A07 rule 5 says a protected failure_detail is returned to an agent "only as its length and that class" without defining what length measures.
open_points.question: Is the disclosed failure_detail length measured in UTF-8 bytes, Unicode code points, or another unit?
options: UTF-8 bytes
Unicode code points
characters after truncation under another defined convention

open_points.subject: fixed MCP surface
open_points.text: K-11 says the fixed surface is "inspect, author, try, run, resume, read traces, and the owner's approve, accept, activate, grant, revoke, resolve and cancel", while the State 0 primary-action table and A16 rule 3 also require callable actions to capture an execution, release a run, roll back a slot, propose a binding, compose and prove a flow, and refuse an effect.
open_points.question: Are the omitted actions separate operations on the fixed surface, aliases or modes of the listed operations, or intentionally unavailable?
options: separate fixed operations
modes of broader listed operations such as author or inspect
not exposed despite the primary-action table

open_points.subject: surface request size
open_points.text: A16 rule 1 counts "the bytes of the request message as received" but does not identify the MCP serialization boundary being counted.
open_points.question: Does surface_request_bytes_max count the complete encoded MCP/JSON-RPC message, only the operation payload, decoded string bytes, or some other byte sequence, and does it include the token and transport framing?
options: complete encoded MCP message excluding transport framing
operation payload only
complete transport frame
open_points.default_guess: complete encoded MCP message excluding transport framing

open_points.subject: token validity
open_points.text: A16 requires every token to be "at least 43 characters (32 bytes in base64url)" but does not say whether base64url syntax is mandatory or what "characters" means for non-ASCII text.
open_points.question: Must tokens be valid base64url strings, and is the minimum measured in ASCII bytes, Unicode code points, or decoded bytes?
options: valid base64url encoding of at least 32 decoded bytes
any string of at least 43 Unicode code points
any UTF-8 string of at least 43 bytes
open_points.default_guess: valid base64url encoding of at least 32 decoded bytes

open_points.subject: failed token-list re-read
open_points.text: A16 rule 2 says an invalid re-read makes every request fail "until a re-read passes" but does not say whether the failed file digest becomes the last-read digest or whether the same unchanged invalid file is re-read on every request.
open_points.question: After a token-list re-read fails, when is another re-read attempted if the configuration bytes do not change?
options: on every subsequent request until one passes
only after the file digest changes again
the kernel stops instead of continuing
open_points.default_guess: on every subsequent request until one passes

open_points.subject: credential secret size
open_points.text: A17 rule 2 says the credential secret file "is read then" and decoded as UTF-8, but neither A17 nor A20 gives a maximum file or credential-value size.
open_points.question: What maximum is applied to a secret file and its decoded credential value, and what exact failure occurs when it is exceeded?
options: add a fixed release ceiling and return credential_unresolved
reuse bounded_text_bytes_max and return credential_unresolved
leave credential files unbounded

open_points.subject: secret and configuration path traversal
open_points.text: A17 requires the configuration file not to be a symbolic link and requires a secret file to be read "without following a symbolic link", but says nothing about symbolic links in ancestor path components or replacement between checking and opening.
open_points.question: Must every path component be opened without following symlinks and the ownership/type/mode checks apply to the same opened file descriptor, or is only the final path entry protected?
options: reject symlinks in every component and validate the opened descriptor
reject only a symbolic-link final entry
allow ancestor symlinks but pin and validate the resolved target
open_points.default_guess: reject symlinks in every component and validate the opened descriptor

open_points.subject: credential text validation
open_points.text: A17 rule 2 rejects a credential value that "holds an empty value or a control character" and removes "one trailing newline", without defining control character or whether CRLF is one newline.
open_points.question: Which Unicode or byte ranges count as control characters, and how are LF, CRLF, multiple trailing line endings, NUL and C1 controls handled?
options: remove one final LF, then reject all Unicode control-category characters
remove one final LF or CRLF, then reject ASCII C0, DEL and C1 controls
apply the HTTP field-value grammar directly
open_points.default_guess: remove one final LF or CRLF, then reject ASCII C0, DEL and C1 controls

open_points.subject: installation multiplicity invariants
open_points.text: A17 rule 1 says the configuration holds "at most one credential for each service" and K-16/M28 say at most one selected instance per service, but no rule states how duplicate service entries or duplicate configuration keys are detected or refused.
open_points.question: What happens at startup when configuration syntax represents more than one selected instance or credential for a service, or repeats the relevant key?
options: startup is refused with a defined installation error
the configuration representation makes duplicates impossible and duplicate serialized keys are rejected while parsing
the last entry wins
open_points.default_guess: startup is refused with a defined installation error

open_points.subject: installation startup checks
open_points.text: A03, A16, A17, A18 and A09 each define conditions that refuse startup, while A16's first-failure convention orders checks inside decisions but no text orders startup checks across those decisions.
open_points.question: When several startup faults coexist, in what order are configuration-file security, parsing, token checks, credential-header checks, data-directory checks, locking and sandbox probing performed, and which failure is reported?
options: one explicitly declared global startup order
decision-number order
implementation-defined order
open_points.default_guess: one explicitly declared global startup order

open_points.subject: ready-node eligibility
open_points.text: A13 rule 2 defines a node as ready "when every input port holds its value" but does not also say that an unmapped node must lack a terminal NodeExecution and must not currently wait; only mapped elements are explicitly protected by "a concluded element is never executed again".
open_points.question: Exactly which existing conclusions and waiting states exclude an unmapped node from the ready set, and when may a service_unreachable or resolved-not_applied element become eligible for another attempt?
options: ready requires all inputs and no terminal conclusion or waiting point, with retries enabled only by resume or resolution
any node with all inputs is ready unless the executor separately special-cases every status
a concluded-node rule analogous to the mapped-element rule applies to all nodes
open_points.default_guess: ready requires all inputs and no terminal conclusion or waiting point, with retries enabled only by resume or resolution

open_points.subject: ordering of derived skip and upstream-failure records
open_points.text: A13 selects the smallest ready node, while rules 4 and 5 conclude nodes that have become skipped_by_guard or upstream_failed; A15 orders records that "become non-executable together" but does not say when those conclusions are processed relative to ready-node execution.
open_points.question: After an execution changes several downstream nodes, are all newly skipped or upstream-failed nodes recorded before another ready node executes, after all ready nodes, or interleaved in one declared global order?
options: close all newly non-executable nodes first in A15 order
execute the smallest ready node first
choose the smallest node across ready and newly non-executable nodes
open_points.default_guess: close all newly non-executable nodes first in A15 order

open_points.subject: map_index numbering
open_points.text: M20, M23, M24, M26 and A13 use map_index to identify and order mapped elements, but no rule says whether the first list element is index 0 or 1.
open_points.question: What map_index is assigned to the first element of a mapped node?

open_points.subject: run with both a failure and a wait
open_points.text: M19 says "The run is failed when no node can run any more and some node failed", while A13 rule 7 ends a run only "when nothing can execute and nothing waits" and A13 rule 8 leaves a run resting while any element waits.
open_points.question: If one branch has failed and every remaining unfinished branch is waiting for approval, service recovery or outcome resolution, does the run end failed or remain awaiting_approval/pending?
options: remain waiting until all waiting points are resolved or the owner cancels/refuses
end failed as soon as no node is currently executable
end failed only for some categories of wait
open_points.default_guess: remain waiting until all waiting points are resolved or the owner cancels/refuses

open_points.subject: successful run with guarded skips
open_points.text: M19 says a run succeeds "when every node and output concluded successfully", while A13 rule 7 treats nodes recorded skipped_by_guard as compatible with success and A05/A13 allow flow outputs reported skipped_by_guard.
open_points.question: Does "concluded successfully" in M19 include skipped_by_guard nodes and flow outputs, or must M19 be narrowed to A13's explicit success rule?
options: skipped_by_guard counts as a successful conclusion
only produced outputs and succeeded nodes permit run success
nodes may be skipped but every flow output must be produced
open_points.default_guess: skipped_by_guard counts as a successful conclusion

open_points.subject: mapped aggregate failure trace
open_points.text: K-09 says "Every node execution writes one immutable trace record", but A13 rule 6 says an oversized mapped output list fails the mapped node and "No record of the node states that failure"; A15 likewise gives a mapped node no record of its own when elements ran.
open_points.question: Is the derived aggregate failure intentionally exempt from K-09's one-record requirement, or must a NodeExecution or another immutable trace record explicitly record the mapped node's aggregate conclusion?
options: the aggregate conclusion is derived and is an explicit exception to K-09
write a mapped-node NodeExecution for the aggregate conclusion
write a distinct immutable aggregate record
open_points.default_guess: the aggregate conclusion is derived and is an explicit exception to K-09
